cards.hint: Think about what pulls without touching.
options: the gravitational attraction of the earth
cards.quote: Weight is the force generated by the gravitational attraction of the earth on any object.
cards.stem: What creates the pull known as weight on any object?

cards.hint: Recall the difference from pushes needing touch.
cards.quote: The gravitational force is a field force; the source of the force does not have to be in physical contact with the object to generate a force.
cards.stem: How can gravity exert a pull when its source is distant?

cards.hint: Think mass combined with local pull strength.
options: the mass of an object times the gravitational acceleration
sum of particle counts near the center
cards.quote: The weight W, or gravitational force, is then just the mass of an object times the gravitational acceleration.
cards.stem: What combination yields the pull near the ground?

cards.hint: Contrast with pulls that act at a distance.
cards.quote: Aerodynamic forces are mechanical forces and the object has to be in physical contact with the air which generates the force.
cards.stem: What sort of interaction needs touch with surrounding air?
